newsitem.title: FRANCE: Michelin shares up sharply on bourse.
newsitem.headline: Michelin shares up sharply on bourse.

text.p: Shares in Michelin were sharply higher on Monday, far outperforming the bourse's blue-chip CAC index after rebounding from losses last week on talk of a capital increase.
Most traders and analysts were unclear what was driving the stock up 2.8 percent at 266.30 francs at 1210 GMT. The CAC-40 index was up one percent.

"The stock fell sharply last week because there were a lot of rumours about a capital increase," one trader said. He said he heard in the market that the company had denied that it would set a capital increase.
He also said a buyer may be driving up the share ahead of a capital increase announcement.
Officials at Michelin were not available for comment.
Car analysts who follow the company said they did not know of a reason for the rise and that the company had consistently denied plans to set a capital increase.

Last week Michelin sold a 2.6 percent stake in PSA Peugeot Citroen, retaining 3.5 percent. PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet told reporters the transaction appeared to reflect a compromise between Michelin's desire to cut debt while keeping good relations with the PSA group, a big client.

The company said in September that its net debt rose in the first half of the year to 23.2 billion francs from 21.6 billion in June 1995 because of a buildup in tyre inventories. It said it had slowed down production to bring down the stocks and its debt in August was below the prior year level.

If subordinated debt is included in overall debt, Michelin's debt-to-equity ratio was 1.97 in the first half of 1996, but if subordinated debt is grouped with equity, the ratio was 1.2 percent, the company said in September.
Michelin's stock was among the biggest losers on the bourse last week, shedding 4.45 percent.
